acceptance.check: Home shows the app shell plus a balance summary card whose hero number is the net position (owed minus owe, viewer currency, largest text on screen) rendered with a direction sentence — 'You are owed' when net positive, 'You owe' when net negative, 'All settled up' when net zero with nothing outstanding — in the matching tone (lent / owed / neutral), with you-are-owed and you-owe totals beside it.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Seed two groups with expenses, sign in, open /: hero figure equals owed minus owe with the direction sentence beside it in the matching tone; totals beside it.

acceptance.check: Per-person rows show who the user owes and who owes the user, each with avatar, name, and words-plus-colour direction; group list shows rich rows with name, member count, per-group balance, and chevron; the left-group notice and the All activity link (the only UI path to /activity) render above the Suspense boundary on the loaded page. Survival through a section failure is proven by the AC-9 unit cases, not by a live failure drive.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Same session: People rows each carry Avatar plus owes-you/you-owe words in lent/owed colour; each group row links to /groups/[id] with count, balance, chevron, words and the sr-only Balance label; ?left=name renders role=status above the boundary on the loaded page; All activity link renders above the boundary and reaches /activity on the loaded page.

acceptance.check: Zero balances read neutral, never debt red: the settled-up sentence renders only when nothing is outstanding (owedMinor is 0 and oweMinor is 0); a net of zero with live rows in both directions renders a neutral figure with both totals visible, the neutral direction sentence, and no settled-up claim; a person row whose cross-group net cancels to exactly zero renders neutral settled-up words with no amount. The hero never carries direction by sign and colour alone. Cross-group totals format in the viewer currency and group rows in their group currency, all through formatMinorUnits with data-amount, words plus colour, never colour alone. The excluded-currency note names every foreign-currency group beside the totals, including a zero-balance foreign group whose row still shows its own zero balance.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Settle a group to zero and check the neutral banner and neutral zero-net person row; construct A-owes-you-100 plus you-owe-B-100 and check the hero shows a neutral zero with both totals, the neutral sentence, and no settled-up claim. Covered by zero-net and net-zero-gross-nonzero unit cases in app/home.test.ts.

acceptance.check: Empty state (zero groups) renders HomeEmpty only — illustration or icon, one sentence on what Tabs does, and a Create-your-first-group button that owns the Create action while groups are empty, with no balance summary card and no People section mounted. alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The notice confirms which group was left; hiding characters weakens that confirmation while wrapping keeps the full name QA's other T-11 branches already assert.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The 80-character limit is validated product behavior shared with group create and rename; changing it for a wrapping defect widens the ticket and moves the goalposts.

work_order.approach: Fix-forward on the PR branch, changing nothing from v1 except the defect: add Tailwind break-words (overflow-wrap) to the LeftGroupNotice paragraph in components/home-panels.tsx — the one-class fix QA's hint names — with no markup, copy, boundary-placement, or data-path change. Add a unit case in app/home.test.ts rendering the notice with an 80-character unbroken name asserting it carries the wrapping treatment, and add AC-11 as the permanent browser contract for notice wrapping. Verify by re-running the exact T-11 repro (/?left=<80 x 'x'> at 375px, document scrollWidth <= 375) plus the existing home suite; no new endpoint, query, token, or dependency.

out_of_scope: Any other v1 scope: the migration itself is proven (12/13 QA tests green), so this order changes only the notice wrapping.

risks: If the PR branch laid the notice out somewhere a lone break-words cannot constrain (e.g. inside a flex row without min-w-0), the class alone may not hold — the 375px scrollWidth assert in AC-11 is the proof, and min-w-0 on the parent is the fallback inside the same one-file edit, not a second ticket.
work_order.root_cause:
The LeftGroupNotice paragraph in components/home-panels.tsx carries no overflow-wrap (no break-words class), so an unbroken 80-character group name in the ?left= notice cannot wrap and forces the document past the 375px phone viewport (measured scrollWidth 753). The v1 plan moved the notice above the Suspense boundary but never named a wrapping treatment for it, so the migrated markup inherited the old plain-

behavior verbatim — correct numbers and structure, one missing overflow class.

cases: an 80-character unbroken ?left= group name renders the leave notice with the wrapping treatment (break-words) so the notice cannot force the layout past the viewport
normal and hostile ?left= values still render as escaped text in exactly one role=status node, and a blank value renders no notice

work_order.understanding:
V1's diagnosis was not wrong, and this is not a re-roll of a mistaken plan: the signed-in Home did need the ui.md migration, PR #45 delivered it, and QA passed 12/13 tests with every acceptance criterion green except AC-5, which fails only on exploratory T-11. What v1 got wrong was narrower and was inside its own spec: it moved the ?left= leave notice above the Suspense boundary but specified no wrapping treatment for it, and the new LeftGroupNotice paragraph — like the old app/page.tsx notice before it — renders the sentence in a plain

with no word-breaking. A group name at GROUP_NAME_MAX (80 characters, unbroken, the exact value the leave flow redirects with) therefore sets the notice's intrinsic width past the phone viewport: scrollWidth 753 at 375px. QA marks BUG-1 introduced_by_pr false — the defect predates the diff — but the PR owns the component now and AC-5's no-horizontal-scroll contract already covers it, so the fix belongs to this ticket, not a follow-up.

issue_snapshot.title: Home dashboard with balances, people and groups
issue_snapshot.body:
A signed-in user sees in one glance whether they owe or are owed, who with, and which group needs attention, with groups as rich rows.

UI face: signed-in user opens Home and sees net position, per-person owes/owed rows with avatars, and rich group rows with the create action always reachable. Contract face: consumes the shell, tokens, and shared rows/cards/avatars/badges/skeletons from piece 1 unchanged; reads the existing home balance and group queries through the current server path with no new endpoint or data shape. Follows docs/ui.md Home screen structure and states exactly.

**Out of scope**
- Any balance-math, simplification, or query change; numbers come from the existing recompute path
- Group page, expense editor, settle-up, members, activity, and profile screens
- Dark mode

Covers: TR-11, S-8
Part of #31.
Depends on #33.

## Acceptance (from the split)
- **IAC-1** Home shows the app shell plus a balance summary card whose hero number is the net position, with you-are-owed and you-owe totals beside it.
- **IAC-2** Per-person rows show who the user owes and who owes the user, each with an avatar, name, and words-plus-colour direction; group list shows rich rows with name, member count, per-group balance, and chevron.
- **IAC-3** Zero balances read neutral (All settled up style), never debt red; every amount renders in group currency from one formatter with words plus colour, never colour alone.
- **IAC-4** Empty state shows an illustration or icon, one sentence on what Tabs does, and a Create-your-first-group button; loading shows skeleton summary card and group rows with no layout shift; failure shows retry and never presents cached balances as current.
- **IAC-5** Primary Create group action is obvious: header button on desktop and thumb-reachable fixed button on phones; cards stack vertically at 375px and lay out up to 1024px.
- **IAC-6** Row hit targets are 44px, keyboard path and visible focus hold, one h1 with heading hierarchy, icons are lucide-react aria-hidden next to text, and the ui.md checklists pass.

## Decisions (recorded by the pipeline)

- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-05T17:15:00.755Z):
  Redesign the user interface only; keep the stack, data model, money rules, TRs and every other decision exactly as they are. Rewrite docs/ui.md into a complete, professional design system for the product this issue describes, following the project's frontend-design and ux skills: the full token set (neutral ramp, surfaces, accent, owed/lent/danger with tints, a type scale, the spacing scale extended where layouts need it, radius, elevation), the font loaded with next/font, one icon set named as a dependency, the shared component specs (buttons, inputs including money inputs, segmented control, list rows, cards, avatars, badges, dialogs and bottom sheets, toasts, skeletons, empty states), the app shell and navigation, and each screen's structure as this issue lays it out (landing, auth, home, group page with sections, expense editor, settle-up flow, members and invite, activity, profile) with its states. Record the redesign as a new ADR.
- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-05T17:32:45.640Z):
  Reviewed: the design system in #32 is approved as written — keep docs/ui.md, the screen structures, the component specs, the tokens and lucide-react exactly as they are, and keep every other decision unchanged. Two things in #32 came from the framework, which is now fixed: it re-recorded the eight existing decisions as ADR-0009 to ADR-0016, and it dropped the 'Added by review and QA' section of conventions.md. Regenerate the brief so the PR carries only the one new ADR for the redesign and keeps the learned conventions. In the brief, give each decision you keep its original title without an ADR number, so it is recognised as already recorded.
- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-05T17:45:31.201Z):
  Same as the last request: keep docs/ui.md and every decision exactly as they are; regenerate only, now that the framework also recognises a recorded decision by the title in its ADR heading, so the success-notices decision is not recorded twice.
